clue.text: A degree of role reversal by composer: nothing should precede wind section intro

indicators.note: says the nothing piece comes immediately before the wind piece

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer

indicators.note: the clue literally asks for the word role to be read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned round
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O
to break wind is to fart

indicators.note: the intro of a word is its opening letter, here of section

explanation.surface: A garbled academic note about a composer's work and a wind section's opening bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversal' signals the backwards role, 'should precede' sets nothing before wind, and 'intro' takes the start of 'section'. The schoolboy sense of 'wind' is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bachelor's in humanities is a first university qualification, one of the commonest academic awards.

clue.text: Later item?

parts.note: later means on some future occasion, and the four letters of the word item can be rearranged into a different word for occasion

explanation.surface: A question about what comes later on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works twice: 'Later' is the plain sense, and 'item' is itself a rearranged word for an occasion, so it is another occasion-word in disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on some future occasion, a synonym of later.

clue.text: Bird in feather once

indicators.note: the bird sits inside the run of letters across the words feather once

explanation.surface: A bird that was once in plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird of rivers and marshes, an example of a bird.

clue.text: See 9
US literature's on playing a dangerous game

indicators.note: playing with letters means toying with them until they form something new

explanation.surface: American writing being put on, perhaps a risky dramatic production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges all fifteen letters of US LITERATURES ON, the S of the possessive included.
explanation.definitionFit: A lethal gamble with a revolver holding one bullet, spun and fired at one's own head.

clue.text: Complain about love when heartless and impotent

indicators.note: about signals the complaint word is turned round

parts.note: to beef is slang for to complain

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its middle, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about a loveless relationship and their own inadequacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns BEEF into FEEB; 'heartless' takes the middle out of 'love', leaving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak and powerless, lacking strength or effectiveness, both senses of impotent.

clue.text: See 1
Clergyman abandons worship finally and sits uncomfortably with criminals

indicators.note: the clergyman gives up a letter, so it is taken away from his title

parts.note: a parson is a parish clergyman

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of worship
sitting uncomfortably means the letters of sits are shifted around

explanation.surface: A vicar who quits the church and sits awkwardly among lawbreakers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' drops the last letter of 'worship' from the clergyman, and 'uncomfortably' rearranges 'sits'.
explanation.definitionFit: People who set fire to property deliberately are lawbreakers.

clue.text: As the Edgware Road begins, a short skirt ends

indicators.note: the beginnings of the three words The Edgware Road are taken

parts.note: a miniskirt is a very short skirt, a mini

explanation.surface: Where a London street starts, a miniskirt stops.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgware Road is a London street; 'begins' takes T, E and R, the starts of the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway or bus terminals are where lines finish, so the plural is ends.

clue.text: Breaking up: dishy royal and baroness

indicators.note: breaking the words up shatters their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Tabloid gossip about a handsome royal and a baroness splitting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' works on UP as well as DISHY ROYAL, though the surface reads 'Breaking up' as a split.
explanation.definitionFit: The respectful form of address used when speaking to a baroness or other titled lady.

clue.text: Drug dealer first to supply writers in journal

indicators.note: the writing pieces are placed inside the journal word

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal

indicators.note: first to picks the opening letter of supply

parts.note: pens are writing instruments

explanation.surface: A diary recording a drug dealer's first deliveries to writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the writers, led by the first letter of 'supply', inside the journal. 'Drug dealer' playfully describes a place that hands out medicines legally.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacy or clinic room where medicines are prepared and given out.

clue.text: O for a big country's American pants!

indicators.note: O for a says the letter O takes the place of an A

parts.note: China is a big country, with the possessive giving S

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising the trousers of a huge nation's American.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the A of CHINA'S to O. Pants is the American word for trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual cotton twill trousers, called pants in US English.

clue.text: Sick home movies, oddly out of state

parts.note: ill means sick
in means at home

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters of movies are dropped, keeping the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Feeling ill at home, watching films, and generally out of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly out' removes M, V, E from 'movies', leaving OIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern US state whose largest city is Chicago.

clue.text: Parapraxis for a fun ride?

parts.note: read the solution as instructions: the first word is a rearrangement of a fun ride, and the second word, meaning go astray, signals that rearrangement

explanation.surface: A psychologist's jargon proposed as a substitute for a fairground thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the second word of the answer acts as an anagram signal applied to the first, which unscrambles to 'a fun ride'.
explanation.definitionFit: Parapraxis is the technical term for a revealing verbal or memory error said to expose the unconscious.

clue.text: Most unpleasant argument from a French line of saints?

parts.note: un is French for a
a row of holy people, a holy row

explanation.surface: A nasty quarrel arising from a French procession of saints.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy, bitter quarrel; unholy here means dreadful.

clue.text: See 13
Pacy movement through long road hazard

indicators.note: the rearranged letters run right through the middle of the yearning word

parts.note: to long for is to itch

indicators.note: movement means the letters of pacy are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A fast car moving along a long stretch of road meets danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' rearranges 'Pacy', and 'through' runs those letters through the word for long, just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen stretch of road surface that makes cars skid, a winter driving danger.

clue.text: Network chaos for Sean Connery?

indicators.note: the actor's famous slurred s, turning a hissing sound into a shushing one, is how the word is pronounced

parts.note: a mess is a state of chaos

explanation.surface: A question about what disorder means for a famous Scottish actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Sean Connery, the Scottish actor, was known for pronouncing S as SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A net or interlaced structure, a synonym for network.

clue.text: Manage to come up with a sci-fi computer that's momentous

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cope is to manage
HAL 9000 is the computer in the film 2001: A Space Odyssey

explanation.surface: Coping with a science-fiction computer turns out to be significant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to come up' turns COPE into EPOC in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking a new era, of great historic importance, so momentous.

clue.text: Time when half of 12 backed one with a parsimonious rule mostly

indicators.note: mostly means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: William of Occam gave his name to Occam's razor, the rule of choosing the simplest explanation

indicators.note: backed means this piece is turned round
half of takes one half of the word, here its second half

parts.note: the answer to 12 across, a US state

explanation.surface: An occasion when a frugal ruler is half supported.
explanation.walkthrough: OCCAM less M gives OCCA; 'half of' takes NOIS from ILLINOIS (12 across) and 'backed' turns it into SION.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular moment or event, so a point in time.

clue.text: Choose mail programme that's just right

parts.note: to opt is to choose

indicators.note: to programme mail is to reorganise it, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Choosing an email program that suits perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Best or most favourable, so exactly right.

clue.text: Romp makes ham actor take 5

indicators.note: the actor anagram takes in the number, holding it inside
a ham performance mangles its material, so the letters of actor are rearranged

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A hammy actor romping through a fifth take of a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' rearranges ACTOR into CAORT, and 'take' puts V (Roman 5) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To leap and prance about boisterously, which is to frolic.

clue.text: Finding out who's there for learners after end of year local trouble

indicators.note: to trouble something is to disturb it, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate letter, twice for plural

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of year

explanation.surface: A local fuss after the school year ends for the learners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges LL, R (end of 'year') and LOCAL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading names aloud from a register to check attendance.

clue.text: Dined by friend showing taste

indicators.note: by means one piece sits beside the other, the friend first

parts.note: a pal is a friend
ate means dined

explanation.surface: Eating with a friend shows good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The palate is the sense of flavour, or discernment, so taste.

clue.text: Flower in position

definitions.meaning: a water lily sacred in Asia

explanation.definitionFit: Both a sacred water plant and a seated cross-legged yoga pose take this name.

clue.text: Temperature master with hot reset

parts.note: T is the scientific abbreviation for temperature

indicators.note: to reset is to set again in a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A device that controls heat, reset when things get too hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reset' rearranges T, MASTER and HOT; the whole clue also describes the device.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that regulates heating automatically, keeping control of how warm things are.

clue.text: See 2
Spill the beans and end the game

definitions.meaning: a referee signals full time on the whistle

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means exposing wrongdoing, and literally a referee's signal that a match is over.
